mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 3% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months with UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency easing, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by >= 0.75% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops by at least 0.75% in one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a compositional shift toward lower-wage employment, which reduces average labor productivity and pressures margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE increases in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An above-consensus rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) of more than 0.4 percentage points month-over-month, sustained for two months, signals persistent inflation, which increases the probability of aggressive central bank tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month + 0.4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.4% for two consecutive months.
